image_description: A small, white weasel (likely an ermine in winter coat) is positioned on a rough, textured rocky surface. The animal has a slender, elongated body, short legs, and a relatively long tail extending to the left. Its fur appears dense and pure white, contrasting with the brownish-grey rocks. The head is small with visible dark eyes, a pinkish nose, and small rounded ears.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small triangular head with pointed snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, exhibiting the characteristic small, triangular shape and pointed snout typical of mustelids.
Both eyes are visible, appearing small, dark, and round, consistent with the species description.
The ears are visible on top of the head, appearing short and rounded, matching the anatomical expectation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Extremely elongated slender body with remarkably fine, diminutive proportions and lightweight build.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is visibly elongated and slender, maintaining a consistent diameter from neck to hips, indicative of the 'tube-like' weasel morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short dense fur in brown dorsally with white or yellow ventral coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The checkpoint specifies brown dorsal fur. This specimen is entirely white (winter morph/ermine). While biologically valid for the class, it strictly fails the specific color description provided in this checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some species turn white in winter (ermine morph).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image perfectly matches the description of the winter morph, showing pure white fur.
The transition from head to shoulders shows a distinct, slender neck section, contributing to the overall elongated appearance.
The visible front and hind legs are very short relative to the body length, keeping the belly close to the ground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short tail relative to body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible and appears shorter than the main body trunk, consistent with weasel anatomy (unlike stoats which have longer tails with black tips, though this distinction can be subtle).

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness or 'haloing' effect where the white fur meets the complex rock texture, suggesting minor segmentation or blending issues common in AI generation, though not severe.
The front right leg/paw merges somewhat indistinctly with the rock surface. The individual digits are not clearly resolved, appearing slightly melted into the substrate.
